newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee prices continue slow slide.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee prices continue slow slide.

text.p: Prices of Vietnam robusta coffee have continued falling slowly and were trading at around $1,090 per tonne FOB Saigon Port on Friday, down from around $1,100 last week, dealers said.
Trade had been quiet over the past week and prices were expected to fall further during the current season, possibly to as low as $900 per tonne.
"The crop is large and there's good supply from Brazil, so not much interest in Vietnam at present," said one trader.
A dealer in Dak Lak province said beans from the new harvest were still facing drying delays because of heavy rains.
"If the weather doesn't improve soon you're going to see coffee trickling in from here instead of flowing," he said.
Traders said, however, the delays were having little impact on the market because of good availability of supplies from elsewhere in Vietnam.
Vietnam's Finance Ministry announced on Friday it was planning an auction on November 11 to buy coffee for Algeria from state firms as a means of repaying debt.
The announcement, carried in the ministry's Finance and Market magazine, was unclear but indicated Vietnam would buy coffee equivalent to some $2.99 million it owes to Algeria.
At free market prices that would be equivalent to around 2,750 tonnes.
